description:
Newly VISIBLE (not newly broken) in s468bc: until #1037 made a ruled refusal a
statement-level event, `t/op/coreamp.t` refused at transpile and produced no
rows at all.  It now produces 9 pass / 46 fail of perl's 778, and what it
produces exposes two unowned things:

(a) `aborted-forms:15: Undefined subroutine &File::Spec::Functions called`.
    The file does `use File::Spec::Functions;` and then calls its imports; PCL
    resolves the CALL to a sub named after the MODULE.  Fifteen top-level
    forms die on it.

(b) 46 failing rows, all in the `&CORE::` family -- `&CORE::close with no
    args`, `&CORE::foo with too many args`, `&CORE::closedir in list context`,
    plus `__FILE__ / __LINE__ / __PACKAGE__ does check its caller`.

Because of (b) the file LOST its expected-divergence registration in s468bc
(the registration bar is all-or-nothing and the reason cited `CORE::given`,
which explains neither (a) nor (b)).  Its rows are now gated one by one in
`baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv` -- 501 of them, and the file is the one that
exceeds the runner's 500-row log cap, so its row baseline is PARTIAL (#1051).
Its 723-row shortfall is deliberately UNEXPLAINED in
`baselines/row-shortfall.tsv`, with the mixture written into the cause.

Attribution before fixing: measure how many of the 723 belong to (a) and how
many to the refusal, rather than assuming.
subject: t/op/coreamp.t: `Undefined subroutine &File::Spec::Functions called` aborts 15 forms, and 46 &CORE:: rows fail
